content: A man who has not passed through the inferno of his passions has never overcome them.
author: Carl Jung
sourceWork: Modern Man in Search of a Soul (1933)
story:
Following his bitter break with Sigmund Freud in 1913, Swiss psychiatrist Carl Jung entered a prolonged confrontation with his own unconscious at his lakeside sanctuary in Küsnacht. Recording his visions in the famed Red Book, Jung mapped the universal archetypes, shadow instincts, and the individuation journey required to integrate one's hidden depths into psychological wholeness.

Confronting the trials of his era, Carl Jung recognized that adversity is the ultimate crucible of the human spirit. Rather than seeking an easy path free from friction, he urged seekers to welcome the struggle as the very forge that tempers courage and character.
reflectionPrompt: When you look back on past hardships, how did navigating them expand your capacity for strength?
